about.title: Paradise Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Paradise sits along a handful of corridors that carry most of the town's traffic — Skyway, Clark Road, Pearson Road, and Pentz Road among them. Butte County's public crash records show dozens of injury collisions each year here, with reports clustering on Friday afternoons as commuters and weekend traffic overlap. Whether you were rear-ended near a shopping center on Skyway or sideswiped on Pentz Road, the aftermath is rarely simple: medical visits, insurance calls, missed work, and a vehicle that needs fixing all happen at once. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects people hurt in car accidents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and attorneys in this network only get paid if your case results in a recovery. Our goal is simply to get you talking to someone qualified, quickly, so you're not figuring out insurance rules and deadlines on your own.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government entity (like a road authority) may share fault, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can flag this early so you don't lose your claim to a missed deadline.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but any percentage assigned to you reduces your payout. Insurance adjusters know this, which is why a recorded statement given too early — before facts are clear — can quietly shrink your claim.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Claim Deserves a Full Look
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, so a claim built only around medical bills may leave real losses on the table. An attorney working on contingency has an incentive to evaluate the full picture before anything is settled.

items.question: I was in a crash on Skyway during Friday rush hour — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up later. Try to document the scene — photos, witness names, the exact location — before memories fade, especially since Friday afternoon traffic on corridors like Skyway can make fault harder to sort out later. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer until you've spoken with an attorney.

items.question: Do I have to give the insurance company a recorded statement right away?
items.answer: No. You're not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and doing so before you understand your injuries or the facts can work against you under California's comparative fault rules. It's generally safer to let an attorney handle those conversations on your behalf.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a road maintained by the town or county?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity, such as one tied to a road on Clark Road or Pearson Road maintained by the county, can carry a much shorter deadline — sometimes as little as six months instead of the usual two years. This is one of the most common reasons people lose the right to file, so it's worth having an attorney check this quickly.
